title: Maximum-pass machine computation
statement: For every CNF formula $\varphi$ over variables indexed by natural numbers, the intercepted maximum-pass machine, started on the binary serialization of $\varphi$, halts after exactly $4|\mathrm{enc}(\varphi)|+6$ steps and outputs the word consisting of $N(\varphi)$ true bits, where $N(\varphi)$ is the variable count.
hypotheses_covered: A CNF formula over natural-number-indexed variables
replaced:
Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with serialization $\mathrm{ser}(\varphi)$ and
its variable bound $N(\varphi)$ (one more than the largest variable index occurring in $\varphi$, or $0$ if no variable occurs). The intercepted maximum-pass machine, run on
$\mathrm{ser}(\varphi)$, halts within $4\,|\mathrm{ser}(\varphi)| + 6$ steps, and
its output is the unary word $1^{N(\varphi)}$.
